chronologyCheck.note: Fused model cost on test cases split by calendar month (drift check, not re-trained).

splitStrategy: Customer-grouped stratified split 70/15/15 (train/val/test). Every customer appears in exactly one split — no identity leakage. Preprocessing fitted on train only; calibration and fusion fitted on validation only; all reported metrics computed on the untouched test split.

fairness.title: New vs established customers
fairness.description: New customers must not be treated as suspicious merely because history is absent. The model receives an explicit 'history unavailable' indicator instead of imputing risk.
fairness.thresholdNote: New = tenure < 180 days OR history unavailable (configurable).
findings: Escalation-rate gap (New / no history − Established (180d+)): 1.0 pts.
Wrongful-suspicion rate (FPR) gap: -0.2 pts — New / no history 0.18% vs Established (180d+) 0.36%.
Missed-abuse rate (FNR): New / no history 26.2% vs Established (180d+) 30.1%.

fairness.title: Low-value vs other orders
fairness.description: Low-value orders are not presumed more fraudulent. Value bands are audited for error-rate parity and cost parity.
findings: Escalation-rate gap (Low value (< ₹1,500) − All other orders): 0.5 pts.
Wrongful-suspicion rate (FPR) gap: -0.1 pts — Low value (< ₹1,500) 0.22% vs All other orders 0.33%.
Missed-abuse rate (FNR): Low value (< ₹1,500) 30.9% vs All other orders 28.3%.

fairness.title: English vs non-English reasons
fairness.description: Hinglish, transliterated Hindi and Devanagari are legitimate customer inputs. Language is audited for disparate error rates; it is never a routing input by policy.
fairness.thresholdNote: Non-English = detected Hinglish / romanized Hindi / Devanagari.
findings: Wrongful-suspicion rate (FPR) gap: -0.0 pts — English 0.29% vs Non-English 0.33%.
